Issued at 151 AM CDT Tue Jul 21 2026

Per recent GOES-19 water vapor imagery and a hand surface 
analysis, a 994 mb surface low pressure system is moving 
eastward through central Ontario early this morning. A cold 
front extends southward away from the center of the low pressure
system through central Wisconsin and across northern Iowa. A 
ribbon of lower 70 degree dew points extends from the middle 
Mississippi River Valley northeastward toward the Door County 
Peninsula ahead of the front. Regional RAOBS and recent AMDAR 
soundings out of ORD/MDW depict an inversion between about 850 
and 750mb above which lapse rates exceed 7 K/km. The resulting 
thermodynamic profile is supporting a broad region of MUCAPE 
>2000 J/kg ahead of the front early this morning. Meanwhile, an 
upper-level short-wavelength trough is racing into the Great 
Lakes region anchored by a seasonably strong upper-level jet 
streak (105kt at 300mb, per the 00Z MPX RAOB). Pressure falls on
the order of 6mb/6hr in eastern Ontario ahead of the low 
pressure system are supporting a 925-850mb low-level jet across 
the Lower Great Lakes, as confirmed by 45 to 50kt of flow at 2km
sampled by the KLOT VWP. 

Over the past few hours, have been watching a roughly 50 mile 
wide area of percolating radar returns first develop in eastern 
Iowa and then cross into northwestern Illinois. The radar 
returns appear to be associated with isentropic ascent (via the 
LLJ) interacting with the base of the capping inversion and are 
prototypical of nocturnal attempts for thunderstorms to initiate
within a steep mid-level lapse rate environment. Thus far, 
attempts for sustained convection have been subdued likely owing
to synoptic-scale subsidence along the right exit region of the
aforementioned upper-level jet streak centered in Wisconsin and
on the northeastern flank of an expansive MCS moving into 
northern Missouri. However, do have concern that continued 
moistening at the base of the cap will eventually allow one or 
two storms to develop at some point early this morning, 
particularly in the 3 to 6 AM window over the Chicago 
metropolitan area as the upper-level shortwave makes its closest
approach. Provided a storm does develop, strong effective shear
(60kt in the convective layer oriented due easterly) would 
support splitting supercells with a threat for damaging hail. 
Will maintain a 30% chance of storms through the morning for 
this threat keeping in mind it equates to a 70% chance a storm 
doesn't develop. 

The threat for storms will end by daybreak as the low-level jet
peels eastward and subsidence increases in the wake of the 
upper-level short-wavelength trough. Winds will gradually turn 
northwesterly through the morning as the frontal boundary works 
through the area, though not before temperatures have an 
opportunity to bounce into the low to mid 80s. Later this 
afternoon, a secondary front will race southward down Lake 
Michigan leading to a northerly wind shift and more noticeable 
drop in temperatures. The southward advection of a seasonably 
cool airmass (850mb temperatures tumbling toward +10C) atop the 
relatively warm waters of Lake Michigan (near +23C) will set the
stage for a rare July lake effect rain shower set-up along and 
behind the front along the northeastern IL and northwestern IN 
shoreline. In fact, would not be surprised for a waterspout or 
two to develop particularly along any focused convergence bands 
overnight. Waves will quickly build in the wake of the front 
leading to a High Swim Risk after sunset at all southern Lake 
Michigan beaches. 

On Wednesday, an upper-level wave embedded in resident broad 
upper-level cyclonic flow will ripple over the Lower Great 
Lakes. Another bout of low-level cold air advection will keep 
temperatures seasonably cold with highs around 70 degrees. Can 
easily envision stratocumulus clouds filling the skies with 
perhaps a few sprinkles by late morning owing to steep low-level
lapse rates outside of continued scattered lake effect rain 
showers. Continued northerly winds down the fetch of Lake 
Michigan will maintain dangerous swimming conditions at all Lake
Michigan beaches through the entire day. 

Wednesday night, the cyclonic shear axis of the aggregate 
upper-level troughing will shift eastward toward Lower 
Michigan, setting the stage for clouds to clear. Overnight lows 
will be cool if not locally chilly with a few upper 40s readings
not out of question near the Wisconsin state line.

Our brief taste of fall during the middle of summer will be 
short-lived as large-scale upper-level ridging begins to 
rebuild across the central United States toward the end of the 
week. Accordingly, temperatures will incrementally increase 
Thursday onward with a return of highs in the upper 80s to lower
90s by this weekend. We continue to see a signal for a 
convective event in the general region sometime in the July 
27-29 timeframe. 

Borchardt
